Do not raise contra just because a report marker appears; only increase contra if the prefix by itself attributes a factual proposition that the rest of the sentence explicitly denies. Verb-final subordinate/relative clauses are especially sensitive: separating them from their finishing verb typically causes large cohesion loss. Rate cohesion loss by how much core propositional content becomes orphaned (small for lost modifiers; large for missing predicates, arguments, or scope-bearing items).

Raise contra mainly when the remainder contains explicit negation, an unambiguous reversal or cancellation, or a subordinate clause that directly negates the prefix's asserted fact.
